# JackedIN and PathProbe — llms-full.txt

> Extended agent context for getpathprobe.com. This file is a documentation-platform convention; it is not part of the llmstxt.org v2 specification. For a short index, use /llms.txt.

Official site: https://getpathprobe.com/
JackedIN: https://getpathprobe.com/jackedin/
Support: service@getpathprobe.com
Current versions: JackedIN 1.2.1, PathProbe 1.2.1.

Use only on networks and devices you own or are authorized to test. Examples use 192.0.2.10 and router1. Do not put passwords on the command line; use JACKEDIN_PASSWORD or a credential reference.

## JackedIN

JackedIN is an SSH, Telnet and serial terminal for Windows 10/11 x64, Linux x86_64, and Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit (arm64). There is no macOS build yet. Run `jackedin` with no arguments for the desktop window. Run it with a command and it stays in the terminal, prints a result, and exits. On Windows, scripts should call `jackedin.com`, not `jackedin.exe`.

Pricing: 72-hour full trial (window, command line, and local API, every feature on). After that, a $19 USD one-time license (launch price; regular $29) for one computer, non-transferable, with one year of updates. Activate with `jackedin license activate` or paste the key in the app. Checkout is handled by Paddle.

Built-in profiles for Junos, Cisco IOS/NX-OS, Arista, Nokia, MikroTik and more. `--vendor NAME` forces a profile; omit it and the prompt or banner picks one, including the pager and error strings.

### Key CLI commands

```
jackedin                     open the window
jackedin --help
jackedin --version
jackedin examples
jackedin ports [--all]
jackedin connect --host 192.0.2.10 --user admin
jackedin connect --protocol telnet --host 192.0.2.10 --port 23
jackedin connect --protocol serial --host COM5 --port 9600
jackedin exec --host 192.0.2.10 --trust-host-key --json --cmd 'show version'
jackedin fleet --inventory FILE [--cmd CMD] [--output json] [--dry-run]
jackedin backup --host H [--vendor ios|junos]
jackedin diff LEFT RIGHT
jackedin scan --host H [--ports 22,80,443]
jackedin ping --host H
jackedin trace --host H
jackedin mcp
jackedin headless
jackedin license status
jackedin license activate KEY
```

`--output json` is the same as `--json`. `JACKEDIN_JSON=1` matches `--json`. `inventory sync` also accepts `--json`. `--template FILE` parses command output with a TextFSM-style template you supply.

### Verified exec, pacing, and prompt detection

Do not pipe commands into `jackedin connect` and assume the work finished. `connect` treats end-of-file on stdin as the end of the session; the device may still be paging.

`jackedin exec` reads every command first (arguments, `--file`, or stdin), then drives one persistent session. It waits until the device prompt returns before sending the next command, and it pages through `--More--`, `---(more)---`, `---(more 57%)---`, `---(more 100%)---`, `---- More ----`, `Press any key`, and `Press <SPACE> to continue`. It reports a structured result. Each command is `{command, ok, output, prompt, matched_error, timed_out, duration_ms}`.

Pacing:

- `--line-delay MS` — gap between lines for exec, a stdin pipe on `connect`, and a multi-line paste. A serial session uses a 100 ms line delay when `--line-delay` is omitted.
- `--char-delay MS` — pause between characters on a slow serial console.
- `--wait-for-echo` — wait until the device echoes a line before sending the next one.
- `!sleep 500` in a command list waits 500 milliseconds and sends nothing.
- `--timeout SEC` limits each wait. Omit it and a line waits as long as the device needs.
- The next exec command is never sent until the prompt returns.

There is no `--terminator` flag. JackedIN treats the device prompt, and those pager markers, as the end of a command. `--prompt REGEX` replaces the prompt JackedIN detects. `--vendor NAME` forces a profile.

On the API and MCP, the same pacing fields are `lineDelayMs`, `charDelayMs`, and `waitForEcho`.

`--dry-run` prints the command plan and sends nothing. It does not connect.

Example:

```
jackedin exec --host 192.0.2.10 --user admin --trust-host-key \
  --json --timeout 8 --cmd 'show version'
```

The password is read from `JACKEDIN_PASSWORD` when `--password` is omitted.

### Coming from plink?

Plink is a fine, free SSH command-line tool. It is the wrong shape for an AI agent talking to a switch.

The PuTTY manual documents `plink -m` as reading a command file, and says that multi-line files are known not to work with certain embedded servers, such as Cisco routers. Plink can also take commands on stdin. In both cases it does not wait for the device prompt or page through `--More--`. The usual workaround is `timeout`, `pause`, or `sleep` between lines.

`jackedin exec` (and the MCP `exec` tool) sends one command, waits until the prompt on `router1` is back, then sends the next. Optional `--json` reports whether each command succeeded. If you already have PuTTY sessions, JackedIN can import them.

Keep plink for Git and for a single remote command on a Unix server. Use JackedIN for device CLI, serial consoles, and agents. Coming in the next release: human approval before any change (show-type commands run freely; the agent cannot approve a change itself).

### Local API and MCP

The local API is off until it is turned on in Settings. JackedIN listens on 127.0.0.1 only (port 47321 unless changed) and requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Do not treat it as a network service to open up.

`jackedin headless` serves the same API (it must still be enabled in Settings). Open, send, read, close, verified exec (`POST /v1/exec` and `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/exec`), and break (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/break`) work without the `automationApi` setting. Scan, wait, ping, traceroute, and `GET /v1/events` follow `automationApi`.

`jackedin mcp` is a stdio MCP server for that API. It dials 127.0.0.1 only. Leave JackedIN open with the API turned on. The token is `JACKEDIN_API_TOKEN` if set, otherwise the token saved in Settings. `JACKEDIN_API_PORT` overrides the port.

Tools: list_sessions, open_session, send_session, exec, send_break, read_session, close_session, wait_for_output, scan_ports, ping_host, trace_host, read_events.

`exec` and `send_break` use the local API token and do not require `automationApi`. wait, scan, ping, trace, and events follow `automationApi`. Prefer `exec` over piping. `scan_ports` tells the caller to only scan devices they are allowed to test.

Client snippet (Cursor, Claude Desktop, and other stdio clients):

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jackedin": {
      "command": "jackedin",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "env": {
        "JACKEDIN_API_TOKEN": "paste-the-token-from-settings",
        "JACKEDIN_API_PORT": "47321"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Coming in the next release (not in 1.2.1): in AI sessions, show-type commands run freely. A command that changes something runs only after a human approves it. The agent can never approve itself. Treat “human approval before any change” as the headline; do not describe this as shipped.

## PathProbe

PathProbe is a command-line network test tool for Linux and Windows. It has no graphical interface and no API. Commands include dhcp, interfaces, env, scan, link, internet, whoami, traceroute, static addressing, and target.

JSON: Free includes `--json` on interfaces, env, link, internet, whoami, traceroute, scan, dhcp status, and license status, plus the dhcp run final JSON summary. Pro adds live `dhcp run --json` events and `--json` on target, static, dhcp release/stop, and profiles.

`pathprobe mcp` is Pro. On Free it prints that the feature is Pro and exits 1. Tools: interfaces, link, scan, internet, traceroute, dhcp_run. Results use `pathprobe.v1`. `scan` and `dhcp_run` need `authorized` set to true.

Pricing: Free is $0. Pro is $9.99 USD one-time, one license per computer, non-transferable, activated online with `pathprobe license activate --key ...`.

Downloads: https://getpathprobe.com/#download
Release: https://github.com/getpathprobe/pathprobe-releases/releases/tag/v1.2.1
SHA256SUMS: https://github.com/getpathprobe/pathprobe-releases/releases/download/v1.2.1/SHA256SUMS
